title: Set a blind diner's water and salt at the clock positions she was told
instruction: Mia is blind. Put her water at 2 o'clock and her salt at 10 o'clock around her plate, as she was told.
context: Blind and low-vision people are told where things are on a table by clock positions read from their own seat: 12 o'clock is the far side of the plate, 3 o'clock is on their right. Seated across from the robot, Mia's 2 o'clock is on the robot's near left, not its far right.
setup: A navy tablecloth (80 x 80 cm) covers the table. A white ceramic plate (24 cm across), taped down, is centred 44 cm in front of the arm bases on their midline, with a bread roll (7 cm) on it. Mia sits at the far end facing the robot; her folded white cane (four 15 cm segments, one red) lies 68 cm out on the midline. A fork lies 24 cm right of the midline and a steel knife (20 cm) 24 cm left of it, both 44 cm out. A plastic water glass (6.5 cm across, 10 cm tall, 200 g) stands 20 cm out, 6 cm right of the midline, and a salt shaker (4 cm across, 8 cm tall, 80 g) 20 cm out, 6 cm left. A teal vase (8 cm across, 16 cm tall) with a flower stands 64 cm out, 28 cm left.
scoring: 0.5 each for the glass and the shaker if it ends upright (under 15 degrees of tilt) on the table, 8 to 25 cm from the plate centre and within 15 degrees of its clock position as Mia sees it. Her 12 o'clock points from the plate centre toward the robot and her 3 o'clock to the robot's left; water is at 2 o'clock (60 degrees from 12 toward 3), salt at 10 o'clock (60 degrees from 12 toward 9). A protractor centred on the plate checks it.
reset_notes: Return the glass and the shaker to their marks.
fidelity: Rigid bodies only. Mia is not simulated; her folded cane marks her seat at the far end of the table. The plate is fixed in place, as it is taped down in real trials. The bread roll is a sphere and the glass a plain cylinder. Every surface has the same rubber-like friction (1.2).
